day_shape: 71 items: CENTCOM says US blockade has redirected 84-85 commercial vessels off Iran, IDF kills Islamic Jihad's Beqaa commander in Baalbek strike, London trial opens over Iran International stabbing, Pakistan deploying jets/troops to Saudi Arabia, Tehran launches Persian Gulf Strait Authority.

threads.label: US maritime blockade and Hormuz authority
threads.summary: CENTCOM said US forces have redirected 84-85 commercial vessels and disabled 4 enforcing a blockade on Iranian ports, while Tehran launched a Persian Gulf Strait Authority to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz. Tanker Trackers reported a US-sanctioned LPG tanker loaded at Kharg Island on 16 May after slipping past the blockade line; IRIB claimed Trump's $40bn Hormuz insurance plan has covered no ships.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon strikes and Hezbollah fire
threads.summary: The IDF said it struck over 30 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon in the past day and killed Islamic Jihad's Beqaa region commander Wael Mahmoud Abd al-Halim in a strike near Baalbek; Lebanese media reported his 17-year-old daughter was also killed. Hezbollah launched a rocket barrage triggering sirens in Kiryat Shmona, three drones were intercepted, and the IDF Arabic spokesperson issued evacuation warnings for Burj al-Shimali, Harouf and Dibel.

threads.label: London trial over Iran International attack
threads.summary: The trial of two Romanian nationals accused of the 2024 knife attack on Iran International presenter Pouria Zeraati opened in London, with prosecutors telling the court the men acted as proxies for Tehran. Coverage ran in the Times of Israel, Jerusalem Post and Iran International.

threads.label: US-Iran nuclear talks signalling
threads.summary: Times of Israel reported Iran said it had responded to an 'excessive' US proposal after Trump warned the 'clock is ticking', while IRIB cited CNBC denying reports Washington had agreed to lift oil sanctions. Defa Press quoted parliament's foreign policy committee spokesman Rezaei saying the negotiating team 'will not shortchange the nation's rights'.

threads.label: Gulf realignment and Pakistan deployment
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Pakistan is sending fighter jets and thousands of troops to Saudi Arabia to help counter Iran, while Iranian FM Araghchi held a phone call with Saudi counterpart Faisal bin Farhan and met Pakistan's interior minister. IRIB cited a Wall Street Journal report saying covert UAE and Saudi attacks on Iran have ended the regional détente.

threads.label: Iran wartime domestic pressures
threads.summary: President Pezeshkian told Iranians to accept inflation and shortages because the country is at war, while police chief Ahmadreza Radan claimed more than 6,500 people had been arrested on espionage charges since fighting began in February. Amnesty International said Iran drove a global surge in executions in 2025, Europol reported 14,200 IRGC-linked posts taken down, and IRIB reported an arson attack on the Mirgeh Nagshinegh gold mine in Sanandaj.

threads.label: Khamenei cultural and mobilisation messaging
threads.summary: Khamenei's office issued a Persian Language Day message and a donation appeal for war-affected citizens, while Defa Press and IRIB carried mass 'self-sacrificing couples' wedding ceremonies in Tehran and a new IRIB programme on the Supreme Leader's writings. Defa Press also quoted a Defence Ministry spokesman rejecting Trump's claims about destroying Iran's defence capabilities.

events.title_en: Bloomberg: Why petrol price is the most important number in American politics. Although petrol makes up a smaller share of American household budgets, its political power can still make or break a presidency. Compared with other economic indicators, Americans see petrol prices almost every day on large signs at petrol stations, and this 'visibility' has greatly amplified its political effect. US presidents are often judged not on the basis of complex economic indicators, but on petrol prices. Even during periods of low unemployment or positive economic growth, rising petrol prices have been able to change public perception of the economy.
